findings.description: L3b's hook-context fail-open write budget is UNSAFE if applied to protocol-state writes. consumeMailbox (hooks/mailbox.js:704-722) appends inbox history, fsyncs, EMPTIES mailbox.json, THEN updates lastInboxSeq / lastReviewRequiredSeq / operator-direct cursors (mailbox.js:719). If that manifest write 'fails open', mail is durably consumed while the review cursor/gate is stale or wrong, and no later hook can retry the same logical update (the mailbox is already empty). Same hazard for outbox/report finalization and the final Stop manifest seq update.
findings.suggestedFix: Limit fail-open STRICTLY to idempotent/advisory manifest writes (turn-observability, the claimNagSeq nag, markArmIntent). consumeMailbox's cursor update, outbox/report finalization, and the final Stop seq/review-required manifest update must stay FAIL-LOUD / transactional (abort-on-failure, do NOT empty the mailbox if the cursor write cannot commit). The cascade relief for these fail-loud writes comes from L3a (immediate steal) + L3c (heartbeat off the lock) reducing contention, not from making them fail open.
findings.resolution: Restricted L3b fail-open handling to advisory/idempotent writes and required consumeMailbox, outbox/report finalization, and final Stop protocol-state writes to remain fail-loud/transactional with dedicated safety tests.

findings.description: The heartbeat-stamp read is under-specified for current call signatures. deriveListenerState(manifest) is a PURE helper that only receives a manifest (hooks/actor-state.js:59-95) and has many manifest-only call sites (hooks/actors.js:660, :1082; hooks/mailbox.js:435). A stamp reader cannot locate <actorDir>/heartbeat from a manifest alone, so those gates would still demote a live listener on stale manifest.lastHeartbeatAt.
findings.suggestedFix: Route stamp reads through the PATH-AWARE wrapper getListenerState(name, crew, stateCwd, opts) (which already has cwd) rather than the pure deriveListenerState(manifest). Keep deriveListenerState(manifest) pure; have getListenerState read the stamp and pass a derived freshness/liveness signal in. Enumerate and update every gate that currently relies on manifest-only liveness (actors.js:660,1082; mailbox.js:435) to go through the path-aware path, OR document why a given manifest-only consumer is safe to leave on the manifest fallback.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan so heartbeat-stamp reads are routed through path-aware getListenerState while deriveListenerState remains pure, and enumerated the affected gates/tests.

findings.description: The plan does not classify manifest-write call sites by safety. Without an explicit best-effort-vs-must-commit table, the implementation can wire the fail-open budget into protocol-critical writes and still satisfy the current ACs while corrupting state (root of F-001).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a table to the plan: BEST-EFFORT/advisory (may fail-open) = turn-observability updateManifest, claimNagSeq nag, markArmIntent; MUST-COMMIT/transactional (never fail-open) = consumeMailbox cursor/drain, outbox/report finalization, final Stop seq/review-required update, the v3.6.2 epoch/PID arm claim. Wire the hook best-effort helper ONLY to the approved advisory sites.
findings.resolution: Added an explicit best-effort versus must-commit manifest-write classification table and constrained the fail-open helper to approved advisory call sites.

findings.description: The file-op-count regression AC is under-specified: it does not name the representative hook(s) and exact fixture inputs, the pre-fix baseline count, the numeric target bound, or which fs operations are counted (open/read/rename/lock create+delete). An autonomous implementer could pick a weak fixture and still pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify: the exact hook fire (e.g. a Copilot/codex PostToolUse on a representative manifest), the counted operation set, the measured pre-fix baseline number, and the asserted post-fix upper bound (strictly lower). Keep the fs-op counter seam TESTS-ONLY (do not plumb through production APIs).
findings.resolution: Amended the plan to specify the exact Copilot PostToolUse turn-observability fixture, counted fs operations, measured pre-fix baseline, post-fix bound, and tests-only counter constraint.

findings.description: A lock-free heartbeat stamp { ts, pid, epoch } must be validated for OWNERSHIP, not just freshness. If the consumer accepts any fresh stamp, an orphan/superseded listener can keep writing a fresh stamp and mask a dead CURRENT listener, weakening the v3.6.2 lastListenerEpoch ownership invariant.
findings.suggestedFix: The stamp consumer must IGNORE the stamp unless its pid AND epoch equal the manifest's current lastListenerPid / lastListenerEpoch; otherwise fall back to manifest.lastHeartbeatAt / treat as stale. Add this to the L3c design and to the heartbeat AC.
findings.resolution: Amended L3c so heartbeat stamps are consumed only when stamp pid and epoch match the manifest's current lastListenerPid and lastListenerEpoch, with risk and AC coverage for orphan/superseded stamps.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Implementation Strategy > L3c / Files to Modify
findings.description: The plan does not require updating all health/list surfaces to consume the new stamp. getMemberHealth computes heartbeat age from manifest.lastHeartbeatAt (hooks/health.js:75) and list-members paths also read it. If recurring ticks stop rewriting the manifest, these surfaces report stale/quiet/dead.
findings.suggestedFix: Add getMemberHealth + the list-members snapshot to the L3c Files-to-Modify and to an AC: they must read the stamp ts (with manifest fallback) so a live-but-stamp-only listener is not reported stale.
findings.resolution: Amended the L3c plan to require getMemberHealth and snapshotCrew/list-members liveness rows to consume the validated heartbeat stamp timestamp with manifest fallback.

findings.description: US-002 should not broadly thread the hook budget through mailbox.js BEFORE the safe/unsafe write classification (F-003) is done; otherwise later stories build tests around an unsafe generalized API.
findings.suggestedFix: Reorder: add the write-site safety classification as the first sub-step of the L3b story (or a tiny preceding story), then wire the best-effort helper to ONLY the approved advisory sites.
findings.resolution: Reordered L3b in the plan so write-site safety classification happens before helper wiring, and constrained fail-open behavior to approved advisory hook sites.

findings.description: L3a immediate dead-PID steal can still stall behind an orphaned .steal mutex. acquireStealMutex (hooks/locks.js:92-119) uses only 30s mtime staleness; a hook killed while holding <lock>.steal blocks the main lock's immediate dead-PID recovery for 30s.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend dead-PID immediate stealing to the .steal mutex path too (same host-scoped dead-PID check in acquireStealMutex), so a dead hook holding the steal mutex does not reintroduce the 30s stall.
findings.resolution: Plan L3a strategy + Risk Areas + a dedicated .steal-mutex orphan AC now require the same host-scoped dead-PID immediate-steal on acquireStealMutex (locks.js:92-119) so a dead hook holding <lock>.steal does not reintroduce the 30s stall.

findings.description: The shared bounded events-tail reader must preserve existing turn-observability semantics: reverse traversal, message-id dedupe (lastObservedAssistantMessageId), and malformed/torn-final-line tolerance (skip a torn last JSONL line). detect-active-bg.js parses a tail-bounded window today; the shared reader must not regress either consumer.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an AC that the shared bounded reader preserves reverse traversal + dedupe + torn-final-line tolerance, and that both detect-active-bg.js and turn-observability.js route through it with their existing behavior intact.
findings.resolution: Added a Bounded-reader-semantics AC requiring readEventsTail to preserve reverse traversal, lastObservedAssistantMessageId dedupe, and torn-final-line tolerance, with both detect-active-bg.js and turn-observability.js routing through it and no regression on existing tests.

findings.description: Threading budget options through every generic JSON writer (writeJsonAtomic/updateManifest) risks accidental propagation into protocol-critical writes. A narrower, safer shape is preferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a narrow 'hook best-effort manifest patch' helper used ONLY at the approved advisory call sites; leave writeJsonAtomic / updateManifest FAIL-LOUD by default. This makes F-001/F-003 safe by construction (default is transactional).
findings.resolution: Covered by the F-001/F-003 amendments: L3b keeps the fail-open helper mechanically opt-in only at approved advisory call sites (markArmIntent/claimNagSeq/turn-observability) rather than a generalized mailbox.js write mode; writeJsonAtomic/updateManifest stay fail-loud by default.

findings.description: 'README.md and/or AGENTS.md' for the Defender-exclusion doc is ambiguous for an autonomous implementer.
findings.suggestedFix: Require the plugin-local plugins/crews/AGENTS.md ops note (mandatory); add to README.md only if operator-facing setup already lives there. Name the file(s) explicitly in the L1 step and AC.
findings.resolution: L1 step + AC now make the plugin-local plugins/crews/AGENTS.md ops note MANDATORY, with README.md only if operator-facing setup already lives there.

findings.description: The heartbeat AC should explicitly require stale-manifest/fresh-stamp behavior through BOTH getListenerState(...) and any remaining direct deriveListenerState consumers (or require eliminating direct manifest-only consumers), plus the stale/orphan-stamp rejection from F-005.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand the heartbeat AC: (a) fresh stamp + stale manifest => live via getListenerState; (b) orphan stamp (pid/epoch mismatch) + stale manifest => exited; (c) stamp-absent (pre-upgrade) => manifest fallback unchanged.
findings.resolution: Covered by the F-005 amendment: the heartbeat AC requires fresh-stamp+stale-manifest => live via getListenerState, orphan/superseded stamp (pid/epoch mismatch) => ignored/stale, stamp-absent => manifest fallback, and pure deriveListenerState(manifest) unchanged.

findings.description: The file-op-count seam may be heavier than needed if plumbed through production APIs.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer unit-testing the new bounded tail reader directly + source/behavior tests proving detect-active-bg.js and turn-observability.js use it. If a counter seam is kept, constrain it to tests only.
findings.resolution: Covered by the F-004 amendment: the fs-op counter is specified TESTS-ONLY (monkeypatch/injected fs inside the test; not plumbed through production hook APIs).
